question: Should ClawHub adopt a blanket public-registry restriction for crypto/blockchain/finance/trading content, or continue the current behavior-based policy that prohibits deceptive or unsafe financial workflows?
rationale: Current main implements behavior-based moderation and scanner consequences, while this RFC explicitly leaves category scope and enforcement severity unresolved; source inspection cannot safely choose that policy boundary.

options.title: Keep behavior-based policy
options.body: Allow legitimate finance and on-chain coordination content while prohibiting deception, unsafe spending, hidden wallet actions, spam, and malicious artifacts.

options.title: Ban broad financial categories
options.body: Exclude crypto, blockchain, finance, and trading content from the public registry regardless of narrower purpose or safeguards.

options.title: Default-deny with exceptions
options.body: Permit documented read-only, educational, identity, registry, or reputation use cases only after review.

recommendation.title: Keep behavior-based policy
recommendation.body: Allow legitimate finance and on-chain coordination content while prohibiting deception, unsafe spending, hidden wallet actions, spam, and malicious artifacts.

likelyOwner.reason: The RFC author owns the recent policy consolidation and has coordinated moderation follow-up with affected publishers.
